routes.title: Terms of Service — BSDC
routes.description: The terms you agree to when you create a BSDC account: what the service is, what you may post, how payments work, and how to leave.
routes.heading: Terms of service
routes.summary: These terms cover the BSDC website and the BSDC Android app. By creating an account you agree to them. They are written to be read before you agree to them, not after.
opening: These terms cover the BSDC website and the BSDC Android app. By creating an account you agree to them. They are written from what the platform actually does, so the words below describe the service you are joining rather than a generic one.

BSDC is a community platform for software developers in Bangladesh. It provides public posts, groups, events, jobs, freelance gigs, learning courses, a marketplace, and direct messaging. The service is provided free of charge. Some features, such as advertising credit and marketplace credit, are paid for through bKash as described below.

You need an account to post, message, order, or apply. You are responsible for keeping your sign-in credentials to yourself and for everything done under your account. One person may hold more than one account, but an account may not be shared. You must be at least 13 years old to use the service. When you sign up you choose a username; it must be available, and it may be reclaimed if the account is inactive for a long period.

What you post is yours. By posting you give BSDC a licence to display, store and distribute it as part of running the service — showing it to the people you chose, in the feed, in search results, and in notifications. That licence ends when you delete the content. Deleted posts and messages enter a 30-day recovery window during which you can restore them; after that they are gone. You are responsible for what you post: you must have the right to share it, and it must not break these terms or the law.

routes.title: Delete your BSDC account
routes.description: How to delete a BSDC account and what happens to your data — from inside the app, from the web, or by writing to us.
routes.heading: Delete your account
routes.summary: You can delete your BSDC account yourself, at any time, without asking us and without explaining why. This page explains the three ways to do it and what is kept afterwards.
opening: You can delete your BSDC account yourself, at any time, without asking us and without explaining why. This page explains the three ways to do it and exactly what happens to your data when you do.

Open Settings (the gear in the top bar), choose “Delete account” under Legal and account controls, read what is deleted and what is kept, then type DELETE to confirm. The app signs you out when it finishes.

Sign in, open Settings, and choose the “Delete account” tab. The panel states what goes and what stays, and the confirm button stays disabled until you type DELETE. This works on a phone, a tablet or a desktop.

If you cannot sign in — you have lost the handset, or the address no longer receives mail — write to the support address below from any address and ask us to delete the account. Tell us the username or the sign-in email so we can find it. We answer within 30 days, and we will confirm when the deletion is done.

disallowComment: Every path here is answered `noindex,nofollow` by the default branch of public.seo_for_path, and scripts/db-prove/t37.mjs fails if the two lists drift. An entry holding an asterisk is a pattern rather than a prefix: `/*/*/edit` is any record's editor, and needs three segments because a member may publish a project whose slug is `edit`, making `/projects/edit` a real permalink that must stay crawlable.
